examples.title: Correct the three-year arrow cycle
examples.situation: Three cards read Year 1 maize, Year 2 soybean and Year 3 wheat, but arrows point Year 1→3→2→1.
reasoning: Read the printed year numbers and crop order first.
Draw Year 1 maize → Year 2 soybean → Year 3 wheat → Year 1 maize.
Under each arrow, add the conditional nutrient, pest-host, root, residue or season purpose.
examples.takeaway: 1 maize → 2 soybean → 3 wheat → 1 maize; the arrows must match the written sequence.

examples.title: Justify the adviser case model
examples.situation: The supplied 10-ha temperate case has low tested N after three maize years. A model proposes soybean → maize → potato.
reasoning: Year 1 soybean is considered for rotation diversity and possible N fixation after checking nodulation and fit.
Year 2 maize uses the field under a crop-specific N plan, not a presumed complete N refund.
Year 3 potato changes crop family and cultivation needs; examine pest history, water, equipment and market before calling it a fit.
examples.takeaway: This is one conditional, three-year teaching model. The correct answer is the reasoned sequence, not the mere names.

examples.title: A different valid answer needs different evidence
examples.situation: A student suggests a suitable legume → maize → wheat, plus a fourth-year clover cover crop.
reasoning: Check whether wheat and clover fit the model season and water supply, and whether the clover occupies a full year or an interval.
Compare N and residue claims with actual harvest and management; do not award a fixed fertiliser credit.
Check equipment, market, pest hosts and what happens before the cycle restarts.
examples.takeaway: Accept if each year and transition is supported by site and management evidence, with clear cover-crop timing. Other evidence-based plans are also possible.

examples.title: A pest example is conditional
examples.situation: Someone says soybean after maize kills every corn rootworm and is therefore mandatory on every farm.
reasoning: Rotation to a non-host can reduce some host-specific pests where they actually occur.
Rootworm species and populations differ; extended diapause or rotation-adapted behaviour can weaken a simple one-year pattern.
An Egyptian field needs local identification and scouting rather than an imported pest diagnosis.
examples.takeaway: Use the example to explain a mechanism, not a guarantee or local pest claim.
